articles.title: The Federal Circuit Extends Sanho to the Section 102(b)(1)(B) Grace Period
articles.content:
2011年《美国发明法修正案》（AIA）大幅缩小了美国专利申请人长期依赖的1年宽限期。根据新法规，宽限期仅适用于保护发明者自己的披露（或源自发明者的披露），或在发明者已公开披露发明的情况下。

联邦巡回法院在NCS Multistage Inc. v. Nine Energy Service, Inc.案（No. 2025-1000，2026年9月14日）的裁决聚焦于何种申请前行为足以触发35 U.S.C. § 102(b)(1)(B)的“公开披露”宽限期。判决明确：私下销售不构成公开披露，即使产品实际交付买家且无保密限制。

关键时间线如下：
专利权人首先面临的问题是2013年2月的临时申请不足以支持最终主张的权利要求。这是个大问题，因为AIA于2013年3月对申请生效，这意味着更窄的宽限期适用于本案。任何依赖2013年6月28日申请的权利要求都是AIA生效后的权利要求，根据AIA § 3(n)(1)，单一AIA后权利要求即可将整个专利置于新的§ 102之下。专利审判和上诉委员会在再审中发现临时申请存在缺陷（TCO AS v. NCS Multistage Inc., PGR2020-00077, 2021年2月18日），联邦巡回法院在脚注中接受了这一观点，双方无异议。（我查阅了临时申请，约5000字，而发明专利约12000字，发明专利的权利要求包含临时申请未提及的具体元素。）

是否构成已有技术？我愿通过两步分析已有技术问题：
1. 第三方活动是否构成§ 102(a)下的已有技术；
2. 若构成，是否有§ 102(b)下的例外排除在外。
articles.summary:
by Dennis Crouch

The America Invents Act of 2011 (AIA) substantially narrowed the 1-year grace period that US patent applicants had relied upon for more than a century. Under the new law, the grace period only applies to protect against the inventor's own disclosure (or those derived from the inventor) or in situations where the inventor had already publicly disclosed the invention.

The Federal Circuit's decision in NCS Multistage Inc. v. Nine Energy Service, Inc., No. 2025-1000 (Fed. Cir. Sept. 14, 2026), focuses on what pre-filing actions are sufficient for a patentee to trigger the "publicly disclosed" grace period of 35 U.S.C. § 102(b)(1)(B). The holding is straightforward: a private sale does not constitute a public disclosure, even where the goods are actually delivered to the buyer without any confidentiality restriction.

Let me set up the key timeline of events

  • July 2012: NCS (the patentee) sells its first AirLock device to Tundra that incorporates major aspects of the invention.
  • August 2012: TCO (an unrelated third party to this case) sells a TDP-PO tool to Apache. This is the potential intervening third-party sale, with further uses during the year.
  • February 5, 2013: NCS files its provisional application.
  • June 28, 2013: NCS files its non-provisional application that eventually led to the patent at issue here. Note that both the provisional and non-provisional are within one-year of that original sale.

The patentee's first problem here is that the Feb 2013 provisional application was inadequate to support the eventual claims. That is a big deal because the AIA became effective for applications filed in March 2013. This means that the new, narrower grace period applies in this case.

Any claim that has to rely on the June 28, 2013 filing is a post-AIA claim, and under AIA § 3(n)(1) a single post-AIA claim is enough to put the whole patent under the new § 102. The Board found the provisional gap in a post grant review, TCO AS v. NCS Multistage Inc., PGR2020-00077 (P.T.A.B. Feb. 18, 2021), and the Federal Circuit accepted the point in a footnote without dispute from either side. (I looked up the provisional application. It is about 5k words compared with 12k in the issued patent, and the issued claims include specific elements not found in the provisional.)

Is it Prior Art? I want to walk through the prior art question in the two step way that I teach it: first, does the third-party activity count as prior art under § 102(a) at all; and second, if so, does an exception under § 102(b) take it back out.

articles.title: Shield and Sword: Sovereign Immunity, Discovery, and Rule 19 After TexasLDPC v. Broadcom
articles.content:
联邦巡回法院今天推翻了因未将专利权人德克萨斯A&M大学列为共同原告而被驳回的专利和版权案件。德州LDPC公司诉博通公司案（第2025-1074号，2026年9月14日）。我认为法院的判决是正确的，尽管它没有正面解决这些案件的难点：州立大学可以授权其专利、分享收益，同时仍可援引主权豁免权使自己的文件不被列入案件。

本案的法官阵容有些特别——陈法官（撰写判决书）与首席法官穆尔和西宾夕法尼亚州联邦地区法院首席法官比松共同组成。该案被推翻的初审判决是由第三巡回法院法官斯特凡诺斯·比巴斯在特拉华州临时受命时作出的。

德州LDPC公司是德克萨斯A&M大学五项LDPC纠错专利和三项软件版权的独家许可方。LDPC编码广泛应用于硬盘和闪存控制器以及Wi-Fi和5G调制解调器中，该技术允许接收方自行发现和修复比特错误，被指控侵权的专利涉及解码器吞吐量和消息存储内存的改进。该技术由基兰·古纳姆在A&M攻读博士期间开发，毕业后他加入LSI公司，试图说服该公司向大学购买许可证未果。他后来离职，2014年末其妻子共同创立了德州LDPC公司来开发和转授权该专利组合。LSI现在是被告方之一。

本案始于德州LDPC公司在2018年起诉博通时未将A&M列为共同原告。当博通在2022年传票传唤大学提供其授权文件时，A&M援引第十一修正案主权豁免权，德克萨斯地区法院撤销了传票。博通将此发现障碍转化为加入动议，称未有A&M参与，法院无法根据规则19(a)(1)(A)“完全赔偿”。其核心论点是乔治亚-太平洋损害赔偿分析要求考虑许可方自己的行为。地区法院最终同意被告方，驳回了该案。联邦巡回法院在上诉中推翻了判决，认为“规则19不是发现工具”。
articles.summary:
by Dennis Crouch

The Federal Circuit today reversed the dismissal of a patent and copyright case that had been thrown out for failure to join the patent owner (Texas A&M University) who had asserted sovereign immunity to stay out of the litigation. TexasLDPC Inc. v. Broadcom Inc., No. 2025-1074 (Fed. Cir. Sept. 14, 2026). I think the court got this right, though it reached the result without confronting what makes these cases hard: a state university can license its patents, take a share of any recovery, and still invoke immunity to keep its own files out of the case.

The judges here are a bit interesting because the panel included Judge Chen (who wrote the opinion) along with Chief Judge Moore and W.D. Pa. Chief District Judge Bissoon. The decision they reversed was by Judge Stephanos Bibas, a Third Circuit judge sitting by designation in Delaware.

TexasLDPC is the exclusive licensee of five LDPC error-correction patents and three software copyrights owned by Texas A&M. LDPC coding is widely used in hard drive and flash controllers and in Wi-Fi and 5G modems: the setup lets a receiver find and fix bit errors on its own, and the asserted patents claim decoder improvements in throughput and message storage memory.  Kiran Gunnam developed the technology as a doctoral candidate at A&M, and after graduating he went to work for LSI, where he tried without success to persuade the company to take a license from the university. He left, and in late 2014 his wife co-founded TexasLDPC to develop and sublicense the portfolio. LSI is now one of the defendants.

The case on appeal started when TexasLDPC sued Broadcom in 2018 without joining A&M as a co-plaintiff. When Broadcom subpoenaed the university for its licensing files in 2022, A&M asserted Eleventh Amendment sovereign immunity and a Texas district court quashed the subpoena. Broadcom then converted that discovery frustration into a joinder motion, arguing that the district court could not "accord complete relief" under Rule 19(a)(1)(A) without A&M in the case. The basic argument was that Georgia-Pacific damages analysis requires consideration of the licensor's own practices. The district court ultimately agreed with the defendant and dismissed the case. On appeal, the Federal Circuit has reversed holding that "Rule 19 is not a discovery tool."
